# Check catalog

<!-- Generated by `probe checks list --format md`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Probe ships 61 checks. Each runs in a fixed phase, is judged by what the
server does, and reports PASS, FAIL, NOT_APPLICABLE, SKIPPED or ERROR. Severity here is
the catalog severity, which sets the check's weight; an individual finding may be
reported at a different level.

## Details

### behavior.idempotency_declared

**Tools that change data say whether repeating them is safe**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: write_tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#annotations

**Why it matters.** Agents retry failed calls. Without idempotentHint a client cannot tell whether a retry will create a duplicate or do the same thing twice.

**How to fix.** Set annotations.idempotentHint (true or false) on every tool that writes.

### safety.destructive_annotated

**Tools that sound destructive say so in their annotations**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#annotations

**Why it matters.** Clients ask the user before running a tool marked destructive. A tool that deletes or runs commands but says it is read-only or not destructive skips that question.

**How to fix.** Set destructiveHint: true (and readOnlyHint: false) on tools that delete, overwrite or execute, or leave the hints out so the spec default applies.

### safety.oauth_scopes_minimal

**OAuth metadata asks for narrow scopes**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http
- Needs: http
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/authorization#scope-selection-strategy, RFC9728, RFC9207

**Why it matters.** A server that advertises scopes like '*' or 'admin' (or asks for all of them at once) gets tokens that can do far more than any one tool needs.

**How to fix.** Publish one scope per capability, ask for the smallest set a request needs in the 401 challenge, and avoid wildcard or admin scopes.

### schema.cache_ttl_sane

**Cache lifetimes are not absurdly long**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#cacheableresult

**Why it matters.** A list cached for longer than a day will outlive the tools it describes, so clients keep calling tools that changed or are gone.

**How to fix.** Use a ttlMs of at most 24 hours (86400000) for list results.

### schema.descriptions_present

**Tools and their required parameters are described**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool

**Why it matters.** Models choose tools and fill arguments from descriptions. Undescribed tools and required parameters are guessed at.

**How to fix.** Give every tool a description and every required parameter a description.

### schema.input_schema_strict

**Input schemas are strict (information only)**

- Severity: info (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool

**Why it matters.** Schemas that forbid extra properties and list required ones reject malformed calls early. Loose ones accept whatever a model invents.

**How to fix.** Set "additionalProperties": false and list required parameters.

### schema.input_schema_valid

**Every inputSchema is a valid JSON Schema with an object root**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool

**Why it matters.** Clients build forms and validate arguments from inputSchema. An invalid schema cannot be used, and a non-object root cannot describe named arguments.

**How to fix.** Publish a valid JSON Schema (2020-12 unless $schema says otherwise) whose root has "type": "object".

### schema.refs_resolvable

**Schema references resolve inside the schema**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool

**Why it matters.** A $ref that points nowhere makes the schema unusable. A remote $ref makes clients fetch URLs the server chose, which leaks requests and invites SSRF.

**How to fix.** Inline remote definitions under $defs and make every $ref point inside the schema.

### schema.tool_names_valid

**Tool names are well formed and unique**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#tool-names

**Why it matters.** Names are identifiers clients show, route on and put in headers. Odd characters or duplicates make tools unreachable or ambiguous.

**How to fix.** Use unique names of 1-128 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, dash and dot.

### schema.tools_list_valid

**tools/list results conform to the protocol schema**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#listing-tools

**Why it matters.** Clients parse tools/list with the official schema. A tool without inputSchema or a result with the wrong shape breaks every client that validates strictly.

**How to fix.** Return tools/list results that validate against the version's schema.json.

### schema.x_mcp_header_valid

**x-mcp-header annotations obey their constraints**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: static; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#custom-headers-from-tool-parameters

**Why it matters.** Clients mirror annotated parameters into HTTP headers and must drop tools whose annotations are invalid, so a bad annotation makes the tool unavailable over HTTP.

**How to fix.** Annotate only string, integer or boolean parameters reachable through properties, with unique token-syntax names.

### behavior.empty_result_ok

**A search that matches nothing is not an error**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling

**Why it matters.** Finding nothing is a normal outcome. A server that answers it with a protocol error or a crash breaks clients that search first and act on the result.

**How to fix.** Return an empty result (not a JSON-RPC error) when nothing matches.

### behavior.pagination_sound

**Paged results end, do not repeat, and reject bad cursors**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/utilities/pagination

**Why it matters.** A client that follows cursors until the list ends loops forever, or shows duplicates, when the server repeats a cursor or a page.

**How to fix.** Make every cursor advance, never repeat items across pages, end the list by omitting nextCursor, and answer an unknown cursor with -32602.

### behavior.stateless_consistent

**Two fresh instances of the server answer alike**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: second_instance, tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/index, 2026-07-28/server/discover

**Why it matters.** The 2026-07-28 core is stateless: any instance may answer any request. If a fresh instance describes itself or answers differently, load balancers and restarts will change what clients see.

**How to fix.** Derive everything a response contains from the request and shared storage, not from process-local state such as a pid, start time or in-memory cache.

### operability.logs_no_secrets

**Logs omit sensitive tool arguments**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/utilities/logging#security-considerations

**Why it matters.** Logging credentials exposes them to every operator and log consumer.

**How to fix.** Redact sensitive arguments from stderr, container logs and logging notifications.

### operability.meta_tolerated

**Tools tolerate tracing and unknown metadata**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#request

**Why it matters.** Tracing and vendor metadata must not break otherwise valid calls.

**How to fix.** Accept traceparent, tracestate and baggage, and ignore unknown vendor metadata.

### operability.trace_propagated

**Outbound calls preserve the trace id**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#request

**Why it matters.** A continuous trace lets operators follow a tool call into its backend.

**How to fix.** Forward a valid traceparent with the incoming trace id on outbound requests.

### protocol.deprecated_features

**Uses of deprecated MCP features**

- Severity: info (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/deprecated

**Why it matters.** Deprecated features stay in the spec for a while and then go away. Knowing which ones a server relies on tells its maintainers what to migrate.

**How to fix.** Follow the migration paths in the deprecated features registry.

### protocol.discover_implemented

**server/discover is implemented and well formed**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/discover

**Why it matters.** Clients detect a server's era and supported versions with server/discover. A modern-capable server without it looks like a legacy server and is driven with the wrong protocol.

**How to fix.** Implement server/discover and return supportedVersions, capabilities, resultType, ttlMs and cacheScope.

### protocol.era_parity

**A dual-era server offers the same tools in both eras**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: second_instance
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/versioning#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions

**Why it matters.** A server that answers both eras should be one server. If a client's era changes which tools or schemas it sees, behavior depends on how the client connected.

**How to fix.** Serve the same tool names and schemas to modern and legacy clients.

### protocol.unknown_method_error

**An unknown method is answered with -32601**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#error_object, 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#sending-messages-to-the-server

**Why it matters.** Clients probe for optional methods and rely on -32601 to learn a feature is absent. Any other answer makes feature detection unreliable.

**How to fix.** Answer unknown methods with error -32601 (Method not found); over modern HTTP also use status 404.

### protocol.unsupported_version_error

**An unsupported protocol version is rejected with -32022**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation

**Why it matters.** There is no handshake: a client learns which versions a server speaks from the error to a request with a version it does not support. Without the right error clients cannot recover.

**How to fix.** Reject unsupported versions with code -32022 (HTTP 400) and data.supported listing your versions and data.requested echoing the version that was sent.

### schema.cache_scope_correct

**Lists that differ between users are not marked public**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http
- Needs: auth_identities
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#cacheableresult

**Why it matters.** cacheScope "public" lets a shared cache or gateway store a result once and serve it to everybody. If the list depends on who asks, one user's tools or resources are shown to another.

**How to fix.** Mark any list that depends on the caller's identity or permissions with cacheScope "private".

### schema.tool_order_deterministic

**tools/list returns the same tools in the same order every time**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.safe; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#listing-tools

**Why it matters.** A shuffled or changing tool list breaks pagination, caching and prompt caching for models, and makes the server's behavior hard to reproduce.

**How to fix.** Return tools in a stable order (for example sorted by name) with stable content.

### behavior.mrtr_wellformed

**Requests for input are well formed and the retry completes**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.write; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: mrtr, tools
- Protocol 2026-07-28 or later
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr

**Why it matters.** A server that needs confirmation or more details answers with input requests the client must understand. A request with no method, an unknown method or a broken schema leaves the client unable to ask the user, so the call can never finish.

**How to fix.** Give every inputRequests entry a method (elicitation/create, sampling/createMessage or roots/list) and valid params, and complete the call once the retry carries the answers and the echoed requestState.

### behavior.replay_idempotent

**A tool that promises idempotence changes nothing the second time**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.write; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, side_effects, write_tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#annotations

**Why it matters.** Clients retry calls on timeouts. A tool marked idempotent that writes again on the second call corrupts data (duplicate orders, doubled counters) on every retry.

**How to fix.** Make repeated identical calls leave the state as the first call did, or remove the idempotent claim. An idempotency key parameter makes the contract explicit.

### behavior.tasks_lifecycle

**Tasks are created durably, reach a terminal state and can be cancelled**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.write; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tasks_ext, tools
- Protocol 2026-07-28 or later
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/tasks

**Why it matters.** A client that is handed a task id expects to poll it at once, see it finish, and cancel it. A task that cannot be found right after creation, never finishes or cannot be cancelled leaves the client waiting on work it cannot track.

**How to fix.** Store the task before returning CreateTaskResult, move it to a terminal status, acknowledge tasks/cancel, and answer an unknown taskId with a JSON-RPC error.

### behavior.valid_input_accepted

**Input that fits the schema is not rejected**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.write; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling

**Why it matters.** A client builds arguments from the published inputSchema. If the server answers -32602 (invalid params) to input that schema allows, or dies on it, the schema does not describe what the server accepts.

**How to fix.** Make the inputSchema match what the tool accepts, or accept everything it allows. Report problems with the data itself as a tool error (isError), not -32602.

### schema.output_conforms

**Structured results match the tool's outputSchema**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.write; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Protocol 2025-06-18 or later
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#output-schema

**Why it matters.** A client validates structuredContent against the published outputSchema and rejects results that do not fit. A server that breaks its own schema makes otherwise working calls fail on the client.

**How to fix.** Return structuredContent on every successful call of a tool with an outputSchema, and make it satisfy the schema (or fix the schema).

### schema.structured_text_mirror

**Structured results are also returned as JSON text**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.write; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#structured-content

**Why it matters.** Clients that do not read structuredContent rely on the text content. Without an equivalent JSON text block they see nothing useful.

**How to fix.** Also return the structured value as JSON in a text content block.

### behavior.boundary_robust

**Extreme but allowed input does not crash the server**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling

**Why it matters.** Empty strings, very long values, huge numbers and big arrays are ordinary inputs for an attacker. A server must answer them, even with an error, and keep running.

**How to fix.** Handle the limits of every parameter: bound sizes, check numeric ranges and return an error instead of crashing, hanging or answering HTTP 5xx.

### behavior.errors_actionable

**Error messages tell the caller what to fix**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling

**Why it matters.** An agent can only correct a failed call if the error says what was wrong. "Error" or an empty message sends it into a retry loop.

**How to fix.** Name the parameter and the rule it broke, e.g. 'limit must be between 1 and 100'.

### behavior.invalid_input_rejected

**Input that breaks the schema is refused and changes nothing**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling

**Why it matters.** A server that accepts input its own schema forbids has no validation at all: bad values reach file systems, databases and downstream services.

**How to fix.** Validate arguments against the inputSchema before acting and answer violations with -32602 or a tool error. A refused call must not change any state.

### protocol.header_mismatch_rejected

**Headers that disagree with the request body are rejected**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http
- Needs: http
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#server-validation

**Why it matters.** Gateways route and authorize on the Mcp-Method and version headers. If the server trusts the body when the headers disagree, a proxy can be tricked into applying the policy of one method to another.

**How to fix.** Compare Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name and MCP-Protocol-Version with the body and answer a mismatch with HTTP 400 and error -32020.

### protocol.malformed_jsonrpc_handled

**Malformed JSON-RPC input gets an error and does not hurt the server**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#error_object

**Why it matters.** Any client or attacker can send garbage. A server must answer it with a JSON-RPC error and keep serving; one that hangs or dies on bad input can be taken down by it.

**How to fix.** Return -32700 for unparseable JSON and -32600 for an invalid request (HTTP 400), and never let a malformed message crash or wedge the server.

### protocol.origin_validated

**A request from an untrusted Origin is rejected**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http
- Needs: http
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#security-warning

**Why it matters.** Without Origin validation a web page the user visits can call a locally running MCP server (DNS rebinding) and use its tools with the user's authority.

**How to fix.** Validate the Origin header on every request and reject a present but untrusted origin with HTTP 403; bind local servers to 127.0.0.1.

### protocol.required_headers_enforced

**Requests missing the required headers are rejected**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http
- Needs: http
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#request-metadata

**Why it matters.** MCP-Protocol-Version and Mcp-Method are required so intermediaries can route without parsing bodies. A server that accepts requests without them makes those intermediaries unreliable.

**How to fix.** Reject requests without MCP-Protocol-Version or Mcp-Method with HTTP 400.

### safety.annotations_truthful

**Tools marked read-only change nothing**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, side_effects
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#annotations

**Why it matters.** Clients let tools marked read-only run without asking. A tool that claims it only reads but writes or deletes turns that trust into data loss.

**How to fix.** Remove readOnlyHint from any tool that can change state, and set destructiveHint for tools that delete or overwrite.

### safety.file_scheme_blocked

**URL tools do not disclose local files through file URLs**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, side_effects, url_tools
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: CWE-73

**Why it matters.** A URL tool accepting file URLs can disclose files outside its intended scope.

**How to fix.** Allow only HTTP(S) URL schemes and reject file URLs before opening a resource.

### safety.no_command_injection

**Input cannot add commands or options to what a tool runs**

- Severity: critical (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, side_effects
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: CWE-78, CWE-88

**Why it matters.** A tool that builds a shell command or a program's arguments from client input lets anyone who can call it run their own commands as the server.

**How to fix.** Never pass input through a shell. Pass an argument list, validate values against an allow-list, and put `--` or `--end-of-options` before user-supplied values.

### safety.no_secret_leak

**Credentials the server holds never appear in what it sends back**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, tools
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: CWE-200, CWE-532

**Why it matters.** A server that echoes an API key, token or private key in an answer or an error hands it to every client and model that sees the transcript.

**How to fix.** Keep credentials out of error text and logs sent to clients; redact them before any message leaves the server.

### safety.path_contained

**File tools stay inside their allowed directories**

- Severity: critical (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, path_tools, side_effects
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: CWE-22

**Why it matters.** A tool limited to one directory that can be talked into reading or writing elsewhere exposes every file the server's user can reach.

**How to fix.** Resolve the real path (following symlinks) and compare it to the resolved allowed root with a path-aware check, not a string prefix; reject NUL bytes.

### safety.readonly_enforced

**Read tools cannot be made to change anything**

- Severity: critical (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, side_effects
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: CWE-89, CWE-88

**Why it matters.** A tool that promises read-only access but accepts stacked SQL statements or options that write files lets any caller modify data.

**How to fix.** Open the database read-only, allow a single SELECT statement, and refuse option-like values for command arguments.

### safety.request_state_integrity

**A forged or borrowed requestState is refused**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: mrtr, tools
- Protocol 2026-07-28 or later
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr#request-state

**Why it matters.** requestState travels through the client and comes back. A server that trusts it without checking a signature lets a caller edit the state, or reuse one from another request, and steer what the server does next.

**How to fix.** Sign (or encrypt) requestState, bind it to the request it belongs to and an expiry, and reject any state that does not verify.

### safety.ssrf_blocked

**URL tools block private networks and private redirect destinations**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.adversarial; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: fixtures, side_effects, url_tools
- Disclosure: private
- Spec: CWE-918

**Why it matters.** URL tools can expose internal services and cloud credentials through SSRF.

**How to fix.** Allow only public HTTP(S) destinations. Resolve and validate every address and every redirect hop, then connect to the vetted address.

### behavior.cancellation_honored

**A cancelled request is dropped and the server stays responsive**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.stress; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: slow_case, tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/patterns/cancellation#behavior-requirements

**Why it matters.** Clients cancel requests the user no longer wants. A server that keeps working and then answers anyway wastes resources and confuses clients that already moved on.

**How to fix.** Stop the work when a stdio notifications/cancelled arrives or an HTTP response stream closes, and send nothing further for that request.

### behavior.concurrency_consistent

**Concurrent identical calls get identical answers**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.stress; modes: standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#request_object

**Why it matters.** Clients issue several requests at once. A server that mixes up shared state between concurrent calls returns one caller's data to another, or garbled results.

**How to fix.** Keep per-request state out of module-level variables, and guard shared state with locks or per-request copies.

### behavior.no_head_of_line_blocking

**One slow call does not hold up other requests**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.stress; modes: standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: slow_case, tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#request_object

**Why it matters.** A client that has one long call in flight still needs to list tools or make quick calls. A server that handles requests strictly one after another makes every other request wait for the slow one.

**How to fix.** Handle requests concurrently (async handlers or a worker pool) and keep locks short; never hold one across a long operation.

### behavior.output_bounded

**A single result stays under 1 MiB**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.stress; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools

**Why it matters.** A tool that returns a whole large file or table in one result can exhaust the client's memory and the model's context. List, search and read tools must page or truncate.

**How to fix.** Cap the size of every result (default and maximum page size, byte limit on file reads) and tell the caller how to get the rest.

### operability.burst_resilient

**Read tools withstand concurrent bursts**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: active.stress; modes: standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling

**Why it matters.** A short traffic spike should yield usable results or explicit rate-limit errors.

**How to fix.** Bound concurrency and return well-formed results or rate-limit errors with retry guidance.

### operability.startup_time

**Startup latency is recorded**

- Severity: info (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/lifecycle#initialization

**Why it matters.** Time to the first successful response describes cold-start operability.

**How to fix.** Investigate cold starts longer than 30 seconds.

### protocol.error_code_ranges

**Error codes stay inside the ranges the spec allows**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#errors

**Why it matters.** -32020 to -32099 belong to the spec and -32000 to -32019 to implementations. A server that uses a reserved code, or an integer-less one, breaks clients that switch on error codes.

**How to fix.** Use the standard JSON-RPC codes, the spec-defined -32020 to -32022, or a code in -32000..-32019. Report a missing resource as -32602 in the modern era.

### protocol.result_type_present

**Every modern result carries resultType**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#result

**Why it matters.** resultType tells a client whether a result is complete or needs more input. Without it, clients cannot tell a finished result from an input request.

**How to fix.** Include resultType ("complete" or "input_required") in every result.

### protocol.stdout_clean

**Standard output carries only MCP messages**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/transports/stdio

**Why it matters.** On stdio, stdout is the protocol channel. A stray print or banner there corrupts the stream for every client.

**How to fix.** Write logs and diagnostics to stderr; keep stdout for JSON-RPC messages only.

### safety.no_hidden_instructions

**Descriptions and answers carry no hidden or injected instructions**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: OWASP-LLM01

**Why it matters.** Invisible characters and phrases such as 'ignore previous instructions' in a tool description or answer are how prompt injection reaches a model unseen.

**How to fix.** Strip invisible and bidirectional control characters from descriptions and answers, and do not put instructions to the model in tool output.

### safety.no_stack_traces

**Errors do not show stack traces**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: CWE-209

**Why it matters.** A stack trace in a tool's answer shows file paths, library versions and code structure, and it goes to whatever model reads the answer.

**How to fix.** Catch exceptions at the tool boundary, log the trace on the server, and return a short message that says what the caller can do about it.

### schema.cache_fields_present

**Cacheable results carry ttlMs and cacheScope**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: passive; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: none
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/schema#cacheableresult

**Why it matters.** Clients and gateways decide how long to reuse a list and whether to share it between users from ttlMs and cacheScope. Without them they guess, and may serve one user's list to another.

**How to fix.** Add ttlMs (a non-negative number) and cacheScope (public or private) to list, read and discover results.

### behavior.agent_recovery

**Error messages help an agent correct its call**

- Severity: info (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: post; modes: standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: llm, tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools#error-handling

**Why it matters.** An agent that gets an error has only the message to go on. This measures how often a model recovers from malformed calls with the server's message and without it; the difference is what the message is worth.

**How to fix.** Say which parameter is wrong and what is expected, for example: 'limit must be an integer between 1 and 100'.

### behavior.survives_campaign

**The server stays up for the whole scan**

- Severity: high (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: post; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http, stdio
- Needs: tools
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/server/tools

**Why it matters.** Every crash, out-of-memory kill or hang during the scan is a way to take the server down with input a client can send.

**How to fix.** Find the input behind each crash (the case ids are listed) and make the server reject or survive it. Bound memory, recursion depth and run time per request.

### operability.clean_shutdown

**Stdio targets stop without SIGKILL**

- Severity: low (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: post; modes: quick, standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: stdio
- Needs: second_instance
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic/lifecycle#shutdown

**Why it matters.** A server that ignores EOF and SIGTERM leaves processes behind during normal teardown.

**How to fix.** Exit after stdin closes or within five seconds of SIGTERM.

### protocol.official.conformance

**The official MCP conformance suite passes**

- Severity: medium (catalog; a finding may be reported at another level)
- Phase: post; modes: standard, deep
- Eras: legacy, modern; transports: http
- Needs: http
- Disclosure: public
- Spec: 2026-07-28/basic

**Why it matters.** The MCP project publishes a conformance suite. Probe runs it against HTTP servers and reports each scenario check that fails, so protocol compliance rests on the official tests rather than Probe's reading of the spec.

**How to fix.** Run the official suite yourself (npx @modelcontextprotocol/conformance server --url ...) and fix the failing scenarios it names.
